content: In cases of vaginal breech birth, there may be potential benefits to delivering the baby rapidly in order to prevent the development of progressive acidosis. However, this potential benefit must be carefully balanced against the risk of trauma that could result from a hastened delivery process. The purpose of this review was to evaluate the impact of expedited vaginal delivery—defined as delivering the baby from the umbilicus to the head within a single uterine contraction—on perinatal outcomes. To identify relevant studies, a search was conducted in the Cochrane Pregnancy and Childbirth Group's Trials Register as of May 31, 2015, along with a review of reference lists from retrieved studies. The inclusion criteria for this review were randomized controlled trials comparing expedited vaginal breech delivery with non-expedited delivery in women undergoing vaginal breech birth. Two independent reviewers assessed the single trial identified during the search to determine its eligibility for inclusion. If additional studies are identified in future updates, two reviewers will independently evaluate the risk of bias, extract data, and verify the accuracy of the data. No studies met the inclusion criteria for this review. The authors concluded that there is currently insufficient evidence to determine the effects of expedited vaginal breech delivery on perinatal outcomes.
